name: Agave Spirit
description: Any spirit distilled from cooked agave, including tequila, mezcal, raicilla and bacanora. Flavours run from bright and peppery to earthy and smoky depending on plant and process.

name: Tequila
description: Mexican spirit distilled from blue Weber agave, made mainly in Jalisco. Tastes of cooked agave, citrus and pepper, and is the base of the Margarita, Paloma and Tommy's.

name: Blanco Tequila
description: Unaged or briefly rested tequila, also labelled plata or silver. Clear, with fresh agave, citrus and pepper notes. The standard choice for Margaritas and most shaken tequila drinks.

name: Reposado Tequila
description: Tequila rested in oak for two months to a year. Pale gold, with cooked agave softened by vanilla, caramel and light spice. Used in richer Margaritas, Palomas and stirred drinks.

name: Añejo Tequila
description: Tequila aged in small oak barrels for one to three years. Amber, with agave under vanilla, dried fruit and toasted oak. Usually sipped or used in Old Fashioned style drinks.

name: Cristalino Tequila
description: Aged tequila, usually añejo, filtered through charcoal to strip the colour. Clear like a blanco but with the vanilla and caramel roundness of barrel age.

name: Coconut Tequila
description: Blanco tequila flavoured with coconut, usually bottled at a lower strength and lightly sweetened. Used in tropical highballs and coconut Margaritas.

name: Mezcal
description: Mexican agave spirit made in nine states, mostly Oaxaca, from many agave species. The agave is usually roasted in earthen pits, which gives the typical smoky, earthy flavour.

name: Espadín Mezcal
description: Mezcal made from espadín (Agave angustifolia), the most widely farmed mezcal agave. Balanced smoke, cooked agave and citrus. The usual choice for mezcal cocktails.

name: Ensamble Mezcal
description: Mezcal made from two or more agave species, either cooked and fermented together or blended after distillation. Often pairs espadín with a wild agave for extra depth.

name: Salmiana Mezcal
description: Mezcal made from Agave salmiana, a large highland agave common in San Luis Potosí. Known for green, herbal and chilli pepper flavours, often with very little smoke.

name: Raicilla
description: Agave spirit from Jalisco and Nayarit, made outside the tequila rules from agaves such as maximiliana and rhodacantha. Often fruity, floral and funky, with light or no smoke.

name: Sotol
description: Spirit from Chihuahua, Durango and Coahuila distilled from desert spoon (Dasylirion), a relative of agave. Grassy, earthy and mineral, with pine and light smoke.

name: Bacanora
description: Agave spirit from the state of Sonora, made from Agave angustifolia (pacifica) roasted in pits. Dry and mineral, with roasted agave and a lighter smoke than most Oaxacan mezcal.

name: Patrón Silver Tequila
description: Unaged 100% agave tequila from Atotonilco el Alto in the Jalisco highlands. Soft and clean, with citrus, fresh agave and a light pepper finish.

name: Patrón Reposado Tequila
description: 100% agave tequila from the Jalisco highlands, rested in oak for a few months. Light gold, with cooked agave, honey, vanilla and a touch of oak.

name: Patrón Añejo Tequila
description: 100% agave tequila from the Jalisco highlands, aged in oak for more than a year. Amber, with vanilla, raisin, caramel and toasted oak over cooked agave.

name: Don Julio Blanco Tequila
description: Unaged 100% agave tequila from Atotonilco el Alto in the Jalisco highlands. Crisp, with sweet agave, lemon and grapefruit notes and a clean, dry finish.

name: Don Julio Reposado Tequila
description: Highland tequila aged about eight months in American white oak. Golden, with cooked agave, vanilla, cinnamon and a soft dried fruit finish.

name: Don Julio Añejo Tequila
description: Highland tequila aged around eighteen months in American white oak. Rich but still agave led, with butterscotch, citrus peel, honey and oak spice.

name: Don Julio 1942 Tequila
description: Añejo tequila aged at least two years in American oak and sold in a tall, slim bottle. Sweet and rounded, with caramel, vanilla, chocolate and cooked agave. Mostly poured neat.

name: Don Julio 70 Cristalino Tequila
description: Añejo tequila aged about eighteen months, then charcoal filtered until clear. Keeps vanilla, honey and toasted oak from the barrel alongside fresh agave and citrus.

name: Casamigos Blanco Tequila
description: 100% agave tequila from Jalisco, rested two months in stainless steel. Soft and slightly sweet, with vanilla, citrus and mild agave. A big seller in the United States.

name: Casamigos Reposado Tequila
description: 100% agave tequila aged about seven months in American oak. Soft and sweet leaning, with caramel, cocoa, vanilla and a light oak finish.

name: Espolòn Blanco Tequila
description: 100% agave blanco from the Los Altos highlands of Jalisco, owned by Campari. Bright and peppery, with sweet agave, tropical fruit and lemon zest. A common well tequila.

name: Espolòn Reposado Tequila
description: Highland 100% agave tequila rested for a few months in lightly charred new American oak. Roasted agave with caramel, vanilla, tropical fruit and brown spice.

name: Olmeca Altos Plata Tequila
description: 100% agave blanco from Arandas in the Jalisco highlands, developed with bartenders and partly tahona crushed. Herbal and citrusy, with cooked agave and a peppery finish.

name: Olmeca Altos Reposado Tequila
description: Highland 100% agave tequila aged six to eight months in former bourbon barrels. Sweet cooked agave with vanilla, orange peel and gentle wood spice.

name: Ocho Blanco Tequila
description: Single estate tequila from the Camarena family in Arandas, with each release made from one field. Unaged, with intense cooked agave, black pepper, citrus and mineral notes.

name: Ocho Reposado Tequila
description: Single estate highland tequila rested eight weeks and eight days in used American whiskey barrels. Agave forward, with light vanilla, caramel and soft spice.

name: Tapatio Blanco Tequila
description: Traditional 100% agave tequila made by the Camarena family at La Alteña in Arandas. Full of cooked agave, with black pepper, olive brine and citrus. A long-time bartender pick.

name: Tapatio Blanco 110 Tequila
description: High strength version of Tapatio Blanco from La Alteña in Arandas, bottled at 110 US proof. Concentrated cooked agave, pepper and citrus that hold up in shaken drinks.

name: Tapatio Reposado Tequila
description: 100% agave tequila from La Alteña in Arandas, rested a few months in used bourbon barrels. Cooked agave with light vanilla, butter and baking spice.

name: El Tesoro Blanco Tequila
description: Tahona crushed 100% agave tequila from La Alteña distillery in Arandas. Unaged, with sweet cooked agave, white pepper, green olive and a mineral finish.

name: El Tesoro Reposado Tequila
description: Tahona crushed highland tequila from La Alteña, aged nine to eleven months in former bourbon barrels. Agave and pepper with soft vanilla, oak and a little smoke.

name: Fortaleza Blanco Tequila
description: Small batch tequila from the town of Tequila, made with brick ovens, a stone tahona and copper pot stills. Cooked agave, olive, butter, citrus and black pepper.

name: Fortaleza Reposado Tequila
description: Tahona crushed tequila from the town of Tequila, rested several months in American oak. Cooked agave with caramel, butter, citrus and sage. Usually poured neat.

name: Siete Leguas Blanco Tequila
description: Traditional 100% agave tequila from Atotonilco el Alto, partly crushed by tahona. Unaged, with cooked agave, mint, earth, black pepper and a long mineral finish.

name: Cascahuín Blanco Tequila
description: Family made 100% agave tequila from El Arenal in the Tequila Valley. Unaged, with cooked agave, earth, citrus peel and white pepper. Popular with bartenders for mixing.

name: Cascahuín 48 Plata Tequila
description: Higher strength blanco from the Cascahuín distillery in El Arenal, bottled at 48%. Dense cooked agave with minerals, herbs and pepper that carry through in cocktails.

name: Cascahuín Reposado Tequila
description: 100% agave tequila from El Arenal, rested several months in used American oak. Earthy cooked agave with light caramel, vanilla and dried herbs.

name: Arette Blanco Tequila
description: 100% agave blanco made by the Orendain brothers at El Llano distillery in the town of Tequila. Clean and dry, with agave, citrus and pepper. A well tequila in many UK and Australian bars.

name: Herradura Plata Tequila
description: 100% agave tequila from Casa Herradura in Amatitán, rested 45 days in American oak. Very pale, with cooked agave, green herbs, citrus and a faint wood note.

name: Herradura Reposado Tequila
description: 100% agave tequila from Amatitán aged eleven months in American oak, longer than most reposados. Copper coloured, with cooked agave, vanilla, butter and cinnamon.

name: El Jimador Blanco Tequila
description: Affordable 100% agave blanco made at Casa Herradura in Amatitán. Crisp, with citrus, fresh agave and a light pepper finish. A common house pour.

name: El Jimador Reposado Tequila
description: 100% agave tequila from Casa Herradura rested two months in American oak. Light gold, with agave, vanilla, toasted nuts and gentle spice. One of the top sellers in Mexico.

name: Jose Cuervo Especial Silver Tequila
description: Unaged mixto tequila from the town of Tequila, made from at least 51% agave plus other sugars. Light and slightly sweet with mild pepper. A high volume well tequila worldwide.
image_query: Jose Cuervo Especial Silver Tequila bottle

name: Jose Cuervo Especial Gold Tequila
description: Gold mixto tequila from the town of Tequila, sold as Especial Reposado in some markets. Sweet and smooth, with caramel, vanilla and light agave. Common in frozen Margaritas and shots.
image_query: Jose Cuervo Especial Gold Tequila bottle

name: Jose Cuervo Tradicional Plata Tequila
description: 100% agave blanco from Jose Cuervo's La Rojeña distillery in the town of Tequila. Clean and peppery, with cooked agave and citrus. A step up from the Especial range for mixing.
image_query: Jose Cuervo Tradicional Plata Tequila bottle

name: Jose Cuervo Tradicional Reposado Tequila
description: 100% agave reposado from La Rojeña in the town of Tequila, rested in oak for at least two months. Cooked agave with vanilla, light oak and warm spice.
image_query: Jose Cuervo Tradicional Reposado Tequila bottle

name: 1800 Blanco Tequila
description: 100% agave blanco from the makers of Jose Cuervo, sold in a trapezoid bottle and also labelled Silver. Clean and lightly sweet, with agave, citrus and mild pepper.

name: 1800 Reposado Tequila
description: 100% agave tequila rested at least six months in American and French oak. Buttery caramel, mild spice and cooked agave with a slightly smoky finish.

name: 1800 Coconut Tequila
description: 1800 blanco tequila infused with coconut flavour and bottled at a lower strength. Lightly sweet, with ripe coconut over soft agave. Used in tropical highballs and Margaritas.

name: Sauza Silver Tequila
description: Unaged mixto tequila from the Sauza distillery in the town of Tequila. Light, with fresh agave, green apple and a little pepper. A budget well tequila for mixed drinks.

name: Hornitos Plata Tequila
description: 100% agave blanco made by Sauza in the town of Tequila. Dry and herbal, with citrus and fresh agave. Widely used as a house tequila in the United States.

name: Cazadores Reposado Tequila
description: 100% agave tequila from Arandas in the Jalisco highlands, rested in new American oak. Smooth, with agave, citrus, vanilla and light wood. The flagship of the stag label brand.

name: Calle 23 Blanco Tequila
description: 100% agave highland blanco created by French-born biochemist Sophie Decobecq. Fresh and fruity, with cooked agave, pear, citrus and pepper. Made with bartenders in mind.

name: Tromba Blanco Tequila
description: 100% agave blanco from the Jalisco highlands, started by Australian and Canadian founders with distiller Marco Cedano. Sweet agave, pineapple, mint and citrus. A staple in Australian bars.

name: G4 Blanco Tequila
description: Blanco made by Felipe Camarena at El Pandillo distillery in the Jalisco highlands, using spring water and rainwater. Very mineral, with cooked agave, pepper and citrus.

name: Código 1530 Blanco Tequila
description: Unrested 100% agave blanco from Amatitán in the Tequila Valley. Clean and mineral, with cooked agave, citrus and a soft, slightly sweet finish.

name: Volcán De Mi Tierra Blanco Tequila
match: Volcan De Mi Tierra Blanco Tequila
description: 100% agave blanco from Moët Hennessy and the Gallardo family, blending lowland and highland agave. Herbal and citrusy, with grapefruit, pepper and cooked agave.
image_query: Volcán De Mi Tierra Blanco Tequila bottle

name: Clase Azul Reposado Tequila
description: Reposado aged eight months in American whiskey casks and sold in a tall hand-painted ceramic decanter. Sweet and rich, with vanilla, caramel, hazelnut and cooked agave.

name: Don Fulano Blanco Tequila
description: 100% agave blanco from the Fonseca family, made with estate grown highland agave from Atotonilco el Alto. Cooked agave, green herbs, citrus and a mineral, peppery finish.

name: Don Fulano Fuerte Tequila
description: The 100 proof version of Don Fulano Blanco from the Fonseca family. Oily and intense, with cooked agave, pepper, citrus peel and minerals. Built to stand up in cocktails.
image_query: Don Fulano Fuerte Blanco Tequila bottle

name: El Tequileño Blanco Tequila
description: Blanco from the town of Tequila made from 70% agave and 30% piloncillo sugar, rested two weeks in American oak. Soft and light, with agave, anise and citrus. The local choice for Batangas.

name: El Tequileño Reposado Tequila
description: 100% agave reposado from the La Guarreña distillery in the town of Tequila, rested about three months in American oak. Cooked agave, vanilla, light caramel and toasted oak.

name: Cabeza Blanco Tequila
description: 100% agave blanco made by the Vivanco family in Arandas and bottled at 43% for mixing. Earthy cooked agave, black pepper, citrus and a dry, slightly briny finish.

name: Mijenta Blanco Tequila
description: 100% agave blanco from the Arandas highlands, made by maestra tequilera Ana María Romero. Floral and fruity, with cooked agave, melon, honey and a gentle pepper finish.

name: Maestro Dobel Diamante Tequila
description: The first widely sold cristalino: a blend of reposado, añejo and extra añejo tequilas filtered until clear. Smooth, with vanilla, caramel, nuts and light agave.

name: LALO Blanco Tequila
description: Highland 100% agave blanco from Eduardo "Lalo" González, grandson of Don Julio González. The brand makes only a blanco: cooked agave, citrus, cinnamon and a clean finish.

name: Teremana Blanco Tequila
description: 100% agave blanco from the Jalisco highlands, cooked in brick ovens and distilled in copper pot stills. Bright citrus, fresh agave and a smooth finish. A large seller in the United States.

name: Lunazul Blanco Tequila
description: Value priced 100% agave blanco from the Tierra de Agaves distillery in the town of Tequila. Clean, with citrus, fresh agave and white pepper. A frequent well choice in US bars.

name: Cimarrón Blanco Tequila
description: 100% agave blanco made by Enrique Fonseca from highland agave and usually sold in litre bottles. Dry and peppery, with roasted agave and citrus. A well tequila in many US cocktail bars.

name: Cazcabel Blanco Tequila
description: 100% agave blanco from a small distillery in Arandas in the Jalisco highlands. Earthy and crisp, with agave, citrus and black pepper. Common in UK bars as a house tequila.

name: Del Maguey Vida Mezcal
description: Espadín mezcal from San Luis del Río, Oaxaca, made by Del Maguey for cocktails. Fruity and smoky, with roasted agave, ginger, cinnamon and tangerine. A standard bar mezcal.

name: Del Maguey Chichicapa Mezcal
description: Single village espadín mezcal from San Baltazar Chichicapam in Oaxaca. Medium smoke with citrus, tropical fruit and a long finish of chocolate and mint.

name: Del Maguey San Luis Del Río Mezcal
match: Del Maguey San Luis Del Rio Mezcal
description: Single village espadín mezcal from San Luis del Río in Oaxaca. Spicy and fruity, with a good amount of smoke, citrus and a creamy, clean finish.
image_query: Del Maguey San Luis Del Rio Mezcal bottle

name: Montelobos Espadín Mezcal
description: Joven mezcal from organically grown espadín in Santiago Matatlán, Oaxaca. Balanced between green agave, cooked agave and wood smoke, with a savoury finish.

name: Montelobos Ensamble Mezcal
description: Joven mezcal that combines papalote (cupreata), espadín and tobalá agaves. Fruitier and more floral than the espadín bottling, with herbs, smoke and a mineral finish.

name: Ilegal Joven Mezcal
description: Unaged espadín mezcal from the Tlacolula valley in Oaxaca. Light smoke with green apple, citrus and white pepper. A gentle, mixable mezcal found in many bars.

name: Los Siete Misterios Doba-Yej Mezcal
description: Espadín mezcal from Santiago Matatlán, Oaxaca, distilled in copper stills. The name means espadín in Zapotec. Citrus, herbs, cooked agave and moderate smoke.
image_query: Los Siete Misterios Doba-Yej Mezcal bottle

name: Derrumbes San Luis Potosí Mezcal
description: Mezcal from wild Agave salmiana in San Luis Potosí, cooked with steam in above-ground ovens so there is little smoke. Green chilli, pickle brine, herbs and minerals.
image_query: Derrumbes San Luis Potosí Mezcal bottle

name: Derrumbes Durango Mezcal
description: Mezcal from cenizo agave (Agave durangensis) grown in the high desert of Durango. Earthy and fruity, with stone fruit, wet clay, herbs and a moderate smoke.

name: Banhez Ensamble Mezcal
description: Cooperative made mezcal from Ejutla, Oaxaca, blending about 90% espadín with 10% barril agave. Fruity and mild, with pineapple, banana, pepper and light smoke.

name: Mezcal Unión Uno
description: Joven mezcal from a group of Oaxacan producer families, made from espadín and cirial agaves. Soft smoke with citrus, herbs and sweet cooked agave. Designed for mixing.

name: Alipús San Juan Mezcal
description: Espadín mezcal from San Juan del Río, Oaxaca, the first village bottling in the Alipús range from Los Danzantes. Fruity and sweet, with roasted agave and medium smoke.

name: Alipús San Andrés Mezcal
description: Village mezcal from San Andrés Miahuatlán, Oaxaca, made mostly from espadín. Rich and fruity, with ripe tropical fruit, earth, cooked agave and a moderate smoke.

name: Rey Campero Espadín Mezcal
description: Espadín mezcal made by the Sánchez Parada family in Candelaria Yegolé, Oaxaca. Bottled at full strength, with roasted agave, citrus, green herbs and clean smoke.

name: Bozal Ensamble Mezcal
description: Oaxacan mezcal blending espadín, barril and mexicano agaves, sold in a rustic ceramic bottle. Citrus and floral notes over smoke, with a warm, slightly sweet finish.

name: 400 Conejos Espadín Mezcal
description: Joven espadín mezcal from Oaxaca and the top selling mezcal in Mexico. Mild and approachable, with soft smoke, cooked agave and a lightly sweet finish.

name: Casamigos Mezcal
description: Joven espadín mezcal from Santiago Matatlán, Oaxaca, sold in a matte black bottle. Gentle smoke with herbs, tamarind, pomegranate and black pepper.

name: Mezcal Vago Elote
description: Espadín mezcal from Candelaria Yegolé, Oaxaca, infused with roasted corn before its final distillation. Toasted corn, honeycomb, smoke and green agave. Strength varies by batch.

name: Amarás Espadín Mezcal
description: Joven espadín mezcal from Oaxaca, sold as Mezcal Amores in some markets. Light smoke with citrus, fresh herbs, mango and cooked agave. Easy to mix.

name: Mezcal Verde Momento
description: Espadín mezcal from Oaxaca made by the Mezcal Amarás team, with labels by changing Mexican artists. Smokier than most well mezcals, with grass, peach and roasted agave.

name: The Lost Explorer Espadín Mezcal
description: Espadín mezcal from the Valles Centrales of Oaxaca, made from eight year old agave. Sweet and herbal, with red apple, ripe fruit and a mild smoke.
image_query: The Lost Explorer Espadín Mezcal bottle

name: The Lost Explorer Salmiana Mezcal
description: Oaxacan mezcal from Agave salmiana harvested at around twelve years old. The most herbal bottling in the range, with green chilli, grapefruit and fresh agave.
image_query: The Lost Explorer Salmiana Mezcal bottle

name: Creyente Joven Mezcal
description: Joven espadín mezcal that blends distillates from the Tlacolula and Yautepec regions of Oaxaca. Soft smoke with sweet agave, fruit and light herbal notes.

name: Bruxo X Mezcal
description: Oaxacan mezcal made from roughly 80% espadín and 20% barril agave, bottled at 40% for mixing. Light smoke with citrus, green herbs and sweet roasted agave.

name: Ojo de Tigre Mezcal
description: Joven mezcal blending espadín from Oaxaca with tobalá from Puebla. Mild and slightly sweet, with gentle smoke, citrus and cooked agave. Made to be easy to drink and mix.
image_query: Ojo de Tigre Mezcal Joven bottle

name: Dos Hombres Espadín Mezcal
description: Joven espadín mezcal from San Luis del Río, Oaxaca. Fruity and smooth, with apple, mango, wood and a moderate smoke. Widely stocked in the United States.

name: El Silencio Espadín Mezcal
description: Joven espadín mezcal from San Baltazar Guelavila, Oaxaca, sold in a black bottle. Made for cocktails, with clear smoke, white pepper, fig and roasted agave.

name: Quiquiriqui Matatlán Mezcal
description: Espadín mezcal from Santiago Matatlán, Oaxaca, bottled for a UK-founded brand. Sweet roasted agave, citrus and steady smoke. A common pouring mezcal in British bars.

name: Empirical Ayuuk
description: Spirit from Empirical flavoured only with smoked Pasilla Mixe chillies from Oaxaca and rested in oloroso sherry casks. Not an agave spirit, but smoky, savoury and fruity like mezcal.

name: La Venenosa Sierra Raicilla
description: Black label raicilla from the Sierra Occidental of Jalisco, made from Agave maximiliana and distilled once. Bright and funky, with citrus, cheese rind, herbs and little smoke.
image_query: La Venenosa Raicilla Sierra Occidental black label bottle

name: La Venenosa Costa Raicilla
description: Green label raicilla from the coast of Jalisco, made from Agave rhodacantha and distilled in a wooden Filipino-style still. Smoky and tropical, with pine and ripe fruit.
image_query: La Venenosa Raicilla Costa de Jalisco green label bottle

name: Estancia Raicilla
description: Raicilla from La Estancia de Landeros in the Jalisco mountains, made from Agave maximiliana roasted in an adobe oven. Fresh and peppery, with green herbs, citrus and hibiscus.

name: Hacienda de Chihuahua Sotol Plata
description: Unaged sotol from Chihuahua, distilled from wild desert spoon plants. Light and clean, with grass, eucalyptus, pine and a faint smoke. The most widely exported sotol.
image_query: Hacienda de Chihuahua Sotol Plata bottle

name: Sotol Por Siempre
description: Sotol from Chihuahua made by a sixth generation family producer from wild desert spoon, pit roasted and double distilled. Earthy and mineral, with wet stone, pine and pepper.

name: Rancho Tepúa Bacanora Blanco
description: Bacanora from Sonora made by the Contreras family from pit roasted Agave pacifica. Dry and mineral, with roasted agave, green pepper and light smoke. Strength varies by batch.
